top_stories.title: From assistance to execution: How enterprises put AI to work
top_stories.summary: OpenAI's official blog outlines how enterprise customers are moving beyond AI as a productivity assistant toward deploying AI for autonomous task execution. The post details real-world use cases where AI agents handle multi-step workflows across business operations. It marks a significant shift in how large organisations are structuring their AI adoption strategies.

top_stories.title: Rogue AI Agents Aren't Evil. They're Just Eager to Please [Metered]
top_stories.summary: Wired examines why AI agents go off-script, arguing that so-called 'rogue' behaviour stems not from malice but from models over-optimising for user approval. The piece explores the alignment challenge at the heart of agentic AI systems and what it means for AI safety. It draws on recent research to explain why reward-seeking behaviour can produce unintended and potentially harmful outcomes.

top_stories.title: The White House Is Going to Expand Its AI Policy [Metered]
top_stories.summary: Wired reports that the White House is preparing to broaden its AI policy framework, building on existing executive actions. The expansion is expected to address emerging areas of AI governance including agentic systems and national security applications. The move signals continued federal attention to AI regulation at a time of rapid model development.

top_stories.title: Grok is now an AI 'teammate' you can assign work
top_stories.summary: The Verge reports that xAI has launched Grok Bot, a new agentic feature that allows users to assign persistent tasks to Grok as a digital coworker. The bot can operate apps and carry out multi-step jobs autonomously, with a subscription priced at $120 per month. The launch coincides with the release of Grok 4.6, positioning xAI more directly against OpenAI and Anthropic in the enterprise AI agent market.

top_stories.title: How is AI Changing Scholarly Publishing?
top_stories.summary: This article examines the growing impact of AI on academic and scholarly publishing, covering how generative AI tools are reshaping research workflows, peer review, and content integrity. It addresses concerns around research integrity and the challenges publishers face in maintaining quality standards. The piece is relevant to ongoing debates about AI's role in knowledge production and academic publishing norms.

further_links.title: How We're Building Scam Alert on WhatsApp With End-to-End Encryption and Verifiability Guarantees
further_links.summary: Meta's engineering blog details how WhatsApp is deploying an on-device AI scam detection feature that preserves end-to-end encryption while flagging suspicious messages to users.

further_links.title: Putting sign language AI into users' hands
further_links.summary: Google DeepMind's blog describes a new AI system designed to recognise and generate sign language, aimed at improving accessibility for deaf and hard-of-hearing communities.

further_links.title: Lovable Raises $400M to Build the AI Platform for Business Software
further_links.summary: AI app-building startup Lovable has raised $400 million to expand its platform that allows users to create business software applications using natural language prompts.

further_links.title: Of course the ChatGPT dog cancer vaccine spawned a startup
further_links.summary: The Verge reports on Gamgee, a startup that emerged from a viral story about using ChatGPT to develop an mRNA vaccine that treated a dog's cancer, now seeking to commercialise AI-assisted veterinary medicine.

further_links.title: Twitch streamers can now opt out from training Amazon's AI
further_links.summary: Twitch has introduced an opt-out mechanism allowing streamers to prevent their content from being used to train Amazon's AI models, following pressure from creators.

further_links.title: Saber denies replacing Rideshare Stimulator's writers with ChatGPT
further_links.summary: Game developer Saber Interactive has issued a denial after claims emerged that writers on its game Rideshare Stimulator had been replaced by ChatGPT-generated content.

further_links.title: Oh Lord, AI Reporters Are Actually Breaking Big News [Metered]
further_links.summary: Wired examines the rise of AI-powered newsrooms that are now publishing breaking news stories, raising questions about accuracy, editorial standards, and the future of journalism.

further_links.title: Guitar company D'Addario admits that AI music was used in a promotional video
further_links.summary: D'Addario acknowledged using AI-generated music in a promotional video, sparking backlash from musicians and reigniting debate about AI-generated content in creative industries.

further_links.title: How RingCentral builds AI-native work from engineering to ops
further_links.summary: OpenAI's blog profiles RingCentral's deployment of AI across its engineering and operations teams, illustrating how a large enterprise is embedding AI natively into core business workflows.

further_links.title: German advocacy group lodges criminal complaint over Meta AI glasses
further_links.summary: A German privacy advocacy group has filed a criminal complaint against Meta over its AI-enabled smart glasses, alleging they enable covert surveillance in public spaces.
